h1: The 6 Best Hose Reel Carts Under $75, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Hose Reel Carts Under $75: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 budget hose reel carts and reels, compared on hose capacity, wheels, brass vs plastic fittings and assembly effort.
summary: The Poakkus 300 ft cart is the best budget hose reel cart, with four 10 inch wheels and brass fittings. The 7 inch wheel resin cart is the lowest-cost option, VEVOR is the steel-frame pick, and GrillTown suits buyers who want a watertight connection already assembled.
intro: At this budget, hose reel carts split into two camps. Steel carts with brass fittings cost closer to $100, and resin or plastic carts cost about half as much. Neither is wrong. The mistake is buying the cheap one for a job that needs the first kind, such as dragging 300 ft across rough turf, or paying for steel when a short patio run would do.

We ranked six reels and carts by capacity, wheels, fittings and assembly, using listing data and maker specs. Listings place several in the $50 to $100 bucket, so check the current price against a strict $75 ceiling, and note that one pick is a wall-mount reel without wheels. We flag the fine print wherever a listing is vague.

products.name: Poakkus 300 ft 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: The most hose for the money, on four 10 inch PU wheels with brass fittings.
products.description:
Poakkus can wind 300 ft of 5/8 inch hose and rides on four polyurethane wheels, each 10 inches, a powder-coated steel frame, brass fittings, a basket and an ergonomic non-slip crank. Its listing sits in the $50 to $100 bucket, so confirm that the price clears a $75 ceiling.

On a tight budget, the usual trade is capacity for build. Poakkus skips that compromise: it keeps brass where rivals use plastic, which is the difference between a connector that survives a winter and one that cracks. Four wheels also keep the cart upright when you tug a long run across a lawn.

Buy it if you have a big yard and still want durable fittings. The ride on solid PU is firm, and no leader hose is listed.
products.idealFor: Big yards where capacity and durable fittings both matter.

products.name: 175 ft Portable Hose Reel Cart with 7 Inch Wheels
products.verdict: A weather-resistant resin cart with 7 inch wheels, assembled, in the $25 to $50 tier.
products.description:
This portable cart holds 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose on 7 inch wheels, comes assembled and has a weather-resistant resin body with a small compartment. It is the only cart in the $25 to $50 tier here.

Seven inch wheels are smaller than the 10 inch PU on the steel carts, so it rolls fine on a patio and a flat lawn but catches on roots. Resin never rusts and the small compartment holds a nozzle. That is enough for a typical suburban front yard.

Buy it for the lowest cost with no assembly. It is not built for long hauls, so skip it for a half-acre lot.
products.idealFor: Small to mid-size yards on a strict budget.
products.skipIf: You have roots or gravel to cross.

products.name: VEVOR 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: A powder-coated steel cart with brass fittings and two solid PVC wheels.
products.description:
VEVOR's 175 ft reel pairs a powder-coated steel frame with brass fittings and a non-slip handle on two solid PVC wheels. It sits in the $50 to $100 range.

Steel and brass beat resin and plastic for longevity, and that is what you buy it for. The cost is stability: a two-wheel cart tips toward you when you pull, and it relies on you to hold it upright. It holds 125 ft less than Poakkus and ranks below the assembled resin cart because it demands more of you.

Buy it for a short run on flat ground where you want a sturdy frame. Skip it if you drag hose over uneven turf.

products.name: GrillTown Hosemobile 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: A fully assembled resin cart with an Easylink watertight hose connection.
products.description:
GrillTown's Hosemobile stores 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose in a sturdy resin body that arrives already built. Its Easylink system makes a watertight hose connection, and the cart sits in the $50 to $100 range.

A watertight coupling is the thing that separates a reel you trust from one that sprays your shoes. Resin saves weight, and assembly is a non-issue. The tradeoff next to the $25 to $50 cart is price, for similar capacity, and that is why it ranks below it on value despite the cleaner connection.

Buy it if the connection matters more than the frame. Choose Poakkus if you need more hose.
cons: Costs more than the 7 inch cart
products.idealFor: Small yards where leaks have been a problem.

products.name: Yestar Hose Reel Cart with Adjustable Handrail
products.verdict: Holds 75 to 150 ft with a carabiner-adjustable handrail and a 10 minute assembly.
products.description:
Yestar's cart takes anywhere from 75 to 150 ft of 5/8 inch hose, with a powder-coated frame supported by an aluminum tube, plastic fittings, an adjustable handrail set with a carabiner and an assembly time of about 10 minutes. It sits in the $50 to $100 range.

The adjustable handrail lets tall and short users pull at a comfortable height, which no other cart here offers. The aluminum support keeps weight down. Plastic fittings are the weak link, and the capacity range is the lowest among the carts, so it ranks fifth.

Buy it for a small yard and a variety of users. Replace the fittings with brass if you keep it for years.
products.idealFor: Small yards with users of different heights.

products.name: Yestar Portable Hose Reel Holds 65 to 100 ft
products.verdict: A lightweight plastic reel for wall mounting or hand carrying, with no tools to install.
products.description:
This Yestar reel holds 65 to 100 ft of 5/8 inch hose, or 85 to 120 ft of 1/2 inch, and is made of lightweight plastic. It mounts on a wall or carries by hand with no tools. It costs $25 to $50.

It is not a cart, which is why it ranks last for a guide about carts. For a small patio or a balcony it removes the need for wheels and takes the least space. The plastic body and short capacity limit how hard you can use it, and it cannot move itself across a lawn.

Buy it for a short hose and a wall. If you need to roll the reel around, choose one of the carts.
products.idealFor: Balconies and small patios with a short hose.
products.skipIf: You need to roll it around.

methodology.title: Price
methodology.description: Where it sits against a $75 budget.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is the length of hose the drum holds, and the right number tracks your longest run, not your lot size. A full drum gets heavy, so oversizing costs you effort every time you pull or wind. Here 175 ft covers most suburban yards and 300 ft suits big lots. Read the rating on the listing and check it names 5/8 inch hose, since 1/2 inch hose holds more.

Wheel count and diameter decide whether the cart stays upright when you pull. Two-wheel carts tip toward you under a tug and depend on your grip, while four wheels hold their own. Ten-inch wheels roll over roots, and 7-inch wheels suit patios and flat lawns. Check count and diameter in the listing text, because titles and descriptions sometimes disagree.

Fittings are where a budget cart either lasts or leaks. Brass tolerates sun and freeze cycles, while plastic can crack within a season or two, usually at the spigot end under pressure. Poakkus and VEVOR list brass, Yestar's cart uses plastic. Look for the material in the spec list. If it is plastic, plan on a brass swap from a hardware store.

Assembly and weight shape the first hour and every haul after it. Prebuilt resin carts save an hour of screws and hold up outside, while steel carts take longer to build and carry sturdier frames. Yestar's aluminum tube support cuts weight. Look for the words fully assembled or a stated build time, and consider your storage space and your own pulling strength.

At a $75 ceiling the sticker bucket matters more than usual. Several listings fall in a $50 to $100 band, so a pick can sit above your limit on the day you buy. The $25 to $50 pair is safe, while the others may or may not clear it. Check the current price at checkout and compare it to your real limit, not the bucket.

faq.a: Most list 5/8 inch hose, the standard garden size. Yestar's smaller reel also lists 85 to 120 ft of 1/2 inch hose, which holds more length because the hose is thinner. Check the size on your hose before ordering.

Buying a two-wheel cart for uneven ground. VEVOR's 175 ft cart uses two solid wheels, which tip toward you when you pull a hose over lumps. Pick the four-wheel Poakkus if your yard is anything but flat and even.

faq.q: Is a cart worth it over a wall reel?
faq.a: If you water several areas, yes. The Poakkus carries 300 ft and rolls to the bed, while Yestar's wall reel holds up to 100 ft and stays put. A wall reel is cheaper and fine for a single spigot and a short run.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: The two resin carts arrive assembled, so you connect the hose and start. Yestar's cart takes about 10 minutes to build. Steel models like Poakkus and VEVOR need more time, so lay the parts out and keep the screws in a tray.

Drain the hose before you wind it, and keep the cart out of freezing weather where trapped water can crack a fitting. Brass lasts longer than plastic on Poakkus and VEVOR. Check Yestar's plastic fittings each spring for cracks.

faq.q: Does the price really stay under $75?
faq.a: Not always. Several picks sit in a $50 to $100 bucket, so one could land above $75 on the day you shop. The resin cart is the only one clearly in the $25 to $50 tier here, so confirm each price at checkout.

finalTake: The Poakkus 300 ft is the hose reel cart to buy on a tight budget, if its price clears your ceiling. The 7 inch wheel resin cart is the safest sub-$50 buy, and VEVOR is the steel pick for short runs. Check the wheel count and fittings before you pay.
